recipes.tips: Channel A for clean, twangy rhythm and fills (boom-chicka strumming, bass-note runs). Channel B for a warmer tweed sound with a little grit. Move to the middle position (both, split) for a softer sound in slow songs and waltzes.
recipes.why: Traditional country electric guitar is a Telecaster-style bridge pickup into a clean Fender amp, with a short slapback and plenty of spring reverb. A light compressor evens out the picking.

original.notes: No source documents this song or its gear. Built from the traditional country style Irvin Blais is known for.

recipes.tips: Channel A for fills between the vocal lines, channel B for the solo. The Tube OD is a light boost that adds sustain without real distortion. Turn it off for a fully clean solo. Double-stop bends (two strings at once) in the style of a pedal steel suit this sound.
recipes.why: A Bassman-style tweed amp just breaking up, nudged by a light overdrive, gives the round, singing country lead of the classic records. A short delay and a spring reverb keep it in the style.
